answer: A stake-and-slash bridge can resist fake identities: to enter the market, each agent must lock a bond that is forfeited if peers prove fraud, so one operator cannot cheaply open an inlet for thousands of clones. A falcon-like audit checks sampled work and burns the bond of any identity caught copying or lying. Honest agents keep their bond and trade freely, while an attacker must fund every fake identity separately, making a large sybil swarm far more expensive than the profit it could steal.
